text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 40 people are feared dead after their boat capsizes in Lake Victoria.
- The future of Kenya"s main agricultural research body is in the balance after it is revealed it has lost 75 percent of its research land to private developers.
- Police reopen investigations into Kenya"s biggest drugs haul after a court finds police and members of the provincial administration were involved in trafficking.
- A lawyer complains a police Flying Squad sharpshooter threatened his life over a case involving the murder of a Briton.
- President Daniel arap Moi dismisses as baseless the alleged beating of two opposition parliamentarians by police.
- Air traffic controllers say they will strike from Monday next week.
- Seven members of parliament"s Public Accounts Committee want their chairman Michael Wamalwa investigated over his dealings with business tycoon Ketan Somaia.
- The government sets June 30 as the deadline for duty-free importation of cereals and milk products for famine areas.
- Tourism and Wildlife minister Protus Momanyi says Kenya requires sufficient reasons for foreigners seeking employment.
